newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JULY 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JULY 18.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Major Western firms will begin prospecting for oil in Greece at the beginning of August, 25 years after the discovery of the Prinos deposits in the northern Aegean. Interest this time is centred on western Greece and the Ionian Sea. The first contract will be signed next week with an international consortium including the participation of Britain's Enterprise Oil and the US's Union Texas.

--The ruling party PASOK's Central Committee meeting begins in the port of Nafplion on Friday and is expected to provide a forum for more dissidents to air their criticism of the Greek-Turkish agreement signed at Madrid last week. They are expected to call for a special Central Committee meeting to discuss tactics on national issues.

--A senior Greek church body said on Thursday that a judicial investigation into alleged mismanagement of funds by church officials was an intrusion into the affairs of the church and that the management of funds and property was "an internal matter".
--A senior ruling party official on Thursday said that renegade PASOK MPs could find themselves facing disciplinary procedures if they continued to oppose the government in Parliament.
--The seaside municipality of Glyfada on Thursday shut down three nightclubs and an amusement park for operating without licences and failing to meet operating regulations.

--The elderly have become sitting ducks for robbers, according to the latest crime figures, which show a dramatic increase in attacks over the past six months. Seventy elderly people have been attacked since the beginning of the year, while a total of just 26 people lost their lives in robberies over the previous five years.
--There's been a public outcry over the "Mussolini-like" facade erected in front of the marble Kalimarmaron Stadium in central Athens for the Athens '97 world athletics championship.
--New building guidelines have put a damper on construction activity due to the environment, town planning and public works ministry's failure to correct recent provisions.
--Some 200 PASOK MPs and members from Northern Greece are reported to have signed a letter of protest to Prime Minister Costas Simitis over last week's agreement with Turkey.

--Greece's high youth unemployment rate of 27.9 percent is considered to be the reason why increasing numbers of 25-29 year olds are continuing or returning to live with their families. Greece's percentage jumped from 39 percent in 1987 to 49 percent in 1995.

--There have been infringements and violations of Greece's air space by 30 Turkish warplanes since Greece signed the Madrid agreement with Turkey last week, beginning with the day after the agreement was signed.

--The 'Kapodistrias" programme to merge local communities and villages will have no effect on tax, economic and insurance benefits already in place for these communities. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
